questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 50° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of two supplementary angles is always 180°.

Smaller angle = (Sum of angles − Difference) ÷ 2

Smaller angle = (180° − 50°) ÷ 2

Smaller angle = 130° ÷ 2 = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two angles are supplementary.

The larger angle is 50° more than the smaller angle.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of supplementary angles = 180°

 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 
 

 x

 
 

 x + 50°

 
 

 180°

**Calculations:**

Let the smaller angle be x.

⇒ Larger angle = x + 50°

⇒ x + (x + 50°) = 180°

⇒ 2x + 50° = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 50°

⇒ 2x = 130°

⇒ x = 130° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is exactly 180°. When placed adjacent to each other, they form a straight line.

Complementary Angles

Two angles whose sum is exactly 90°. For example, 40° and 50° form a complementary pair.

Adjacent Angles

Angles that share a common vertex and a common boundary side, but have no overlapping interior area.

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two straight lines intersect, the non-adjacent opposite angles formed are always equal.
</p

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 17 cm, BC = 8 cm, CD = 9 cm, AD = 12 cm, and AC = 15 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Diagonal AC divides the quadrilateral into two right-angled triangles: ΔABC and ΔADC.

In ΔABC (sides 8 cm, 15 cm, 17 cm), 8² + 15² = 17² ⇒ Area = (1/2) × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

In ΔADC (sides 9 cm, 12 cm, 15 cm), 9² + 12² = 15² ⇒ Area = (1/2) × 9 × 12 = 54 cm².

Total Area = Area of ΔABC + Area of ΔADC = 60 + 54 = 114 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 114 cm².**

questions.question: The larger of two supplementary angles is 28° more than the smaller one. The smaller angle (in degree) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two angles with a given sum and difference, Smaller angle = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2.

The sum of supplementary angles is always 180°.

⇒ Smaller angle = (180° − 28°) ÷ 2

⇒ Smaller angle = 152° ÷ 2 = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The two angles are supplementary.

The larger angle is 28° more than the smaller angle.

**Concept Used:**

The sum of two supplementary angles is always 180°.

 
• 
 
 
• 
 
 

 
 

 
 x
 x + 28°
 
 

 Sum = 180° (Supplementary Angles)
 

**Calculation:**

Let the smaller angle be x.

⇒ Larger angle = x + 28°

According to the concept of supplementary angles:

⇒ x + (x + 28°) = 180°

⇒ 2x + 28° = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 28°

⇒ 2x = 152°

⇒ x = 152° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 76°

**∴ The correct answer is 76°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angles

Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to exactly 180°. They form a straight line when placed adjacent to each other.

Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their combined sum equals exactly 90°, forming a right angle.

Linear Pair Axiom

If a ray stands on a straight line, then the sum of the two adjacent angles so formed is exactly 180°.
</p

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f6df85bb678d4030b9f025ad2b98108a24cc1b9378ff5943eebe2ebcbe93d04f.png] **

In Δ ABC:

∠ACB = 180° - (∠ABC + ∠BAC) = 180° - (69° + 23°) = 180° - 92° = 88°

Since AD ∥ BC,

So, ∠ACB = ∠CAD = 88°

Now, In Δ ACD:

AC = CD, So ∠CAD = ∠ADC

questions.question: If ∆ ABC ∼ ∆ XYZ, AB = 6 cm, XY = 8 cm, YZ = 12 cm and ZX = 16 cm, then find the perimeter of ∆ ABC.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∆ABC ~ ∆XYZ

AB = 6 cm, XY = 8 cm

YZ = 12 cm, ZX = 16 cm

**Formula used:**

If two triangles are similar, their corresponding sides are proportional:

AB/XY = BC/YZ = AC/ZX

Perimeter of ∆ABC = AB + BC + AC

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/45671581f2ff703e7eaec774b2466a8a93d24061d8f455e7e9d65f7566247cf8.png] 

AB/XY = BC/YZ = AC/ZX

⇒ 6/8 = BC/12 = AC/16

First, find BC:

⇒ 6/8 = BC/12

⇒ BC = (6 × 12)/8 = 9 cm

AC:

⇒ 6/8 = AC/16

⇒ AC = (6 × 16)/8 = 12 cm

Now, calculate the perimeter of ∆ABC:

⇒ Perimeter = AB + BC + AC

⇒ Perimeter = 6 + 9 + 12

⇒ Perimeter = 27 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: For a regular polygon, the sum of the interior angles is 250% more than the sum of its exterior angles. Each interior angle of the polygon measures x°. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
Given:

The sum of all interior angle of polygon 250% more than the sum of exterior angles.

Formula used:

The sum of all interior angle of a polygon = (n - 2) × 180°

Where n = number of sides

Calculation:

According to question,

Sum if interior angles of polygon 250% more than the sum of exterior angles.

i.e. 350% of 360°

= 350% of 360°

= 3.5 × 360°

= 1260°

The sum of all interior angle of a polygon = (n - 2) × 180°

⇒ 1260° = (n - 2) × 180°

⇒ (1260°/180°) = (n - 2)

⇒ 7 = n - 2

⇒ n = 9

Now, each interior angle x = 1260°/9 = 140°

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: The ratio of the lengths of two corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 15 : 14. The ratio of the areas of these two triangles, in the order mentioned, is:

⇒ Ratio of Areas = (15 : 14)²

⇒ Ratio of Areas = (15)² : (14)²

⇒ Ratio of Areas = 225 : 196

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Let AB and CD be two parallel lines and PQ be a transversal, such that PQ intersects AB at the point R and CD at the point S. If ∠ARP = 2x°, ∠ARQ = y° and ∠DSP = 4x°, then find the values of x and y, respectively.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB and CD are two parallel lines.

PQ is a transversal intersecting AB at R and CD at S.

∠ARP = 2xº

∠ARQ = yº

∠DSP = 4xº

**Formula Used:**

Using the property of parallel lines, corresponding angles and linear pair property:

1. Corresponding angles are equal.

2. Sum of angles on a straight line is 180º.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fe07c7e7ddf1a18c89eb676ae731ec0a68a53b27c92ab87051d5cc6c1e73d30.png] 

Since AB || CD and PQ is a transversal:

∠DSP corresponds to ∠BRP. Hence:

⇒ ∠BRP = 4x° 

Using the linear pair property at point R:

∠ARP + ∠BRP = 180º

⇒ 2x + 4x = 180

⇒ 6x = 180

⇒ x = 30

Using the linear pair property at point R:

∠ARP + ∠ARQ = 180º

⇒ 2x + y = 180

Substitute x = 30:

⇒ 2(30) + y = 180

⇒ 60 + y = 180

⇒ y = 120

**The values of x and y are 30 and 120 respectively.**

questions.question: Select the correct statement regarding the properties of diagonals of a rhombus.

options.text: The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, intersect at right angles and bisect each other
The diagonals of a rhombus are not equal, intersect at right angles and bisect each other.
The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, intersect at right angles and do not bisect each other
The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, do not intersect at right angles and bisect each other

questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to select the correct statement about the properties of diagonals of a rhombus.

**Formula used:**

Properties of rhombus:

 The diagonals are not equal.
 
• The diagonals intersect at right angles (90°).
 
• The diagonals bisect each other.

**Calculation:**

Option 1: The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, intersect at right angles, and bisect each other. (Incorrect, diagonals are not equal)

Option 2: The diagonals of a rhombus are not equal, intersect at right angles, and bisect each other. (Correct, matches the properties of a rhombus)

Option 3: The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, intersect at right angles, and do not bisect each other. (Incorrect, diagonals do bisect each other)

Option 4: The diagonals of a rhombus are equal, do not intersect at right angles, and bisect each other. (Incorrect, diagonals are not equal and they intersect at right angles)

**∴ The correct answer is Option 2.**

questions.question: A chord AB is drawn in a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. If the shortest distance between the centre and the chord is 4.5 cm, then find the length of chord AB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 6 cm

Shortest distance from the center to the chord (d) = 4.5 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e072711c8266d8f9c500beed07652e856a3f0e4c87442edc06e3b23a038cc142.png] 

Let the length of the chord AB be 2x. The perpendicular from the centre O to the chord bisects the chord, so each half of the chord is of length x.

Now, in right-angled triangle OMA (where M is the midpoint of the chord),

OM = 4.5 cm (distance from the centre to the chord),

OA = 6 cm (radius of the circle),

AM = x (half of the chord length).

Using the Pythagoras theorem in triangle OMA:

OA² = OM² + AM²

⇒ 6² = 4.5² + x²

⇒ 36 = 20.25 + x²

⇒ x² = 36 - 20.25

⇒ x² = 15.75

⇒ x = sqrt{15.75} = sqrt{(1575)/(100)} = sqrt{dfrac{63}{4}} = dfrac{sqrt{63}}{2}=(3sqrt7)/(2)

Therefore, the length of the chord AB is 2x = 2 times dfrac{3sqrt7}{2} = 3sqrt7 {cm}

**∴ The length of the chord AB is 3√7 cm.**

questions.question: A tangent is drawn from point P to a circle with centre O. The radius of the circle is 7 cm, and the distance from point P to the centre O is 25 cm. What is the length of the tangent from point P to the point of tangency?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius (r) = 7 cm

Distance from point P to the centre O (OP) = 25 cm

**Formula used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9301f86894a6de8a61f4cee3545c963e26c2aa981b0c1621510da9160b177533.png] 

In a right-angled triangle, Pythagoras theorem:

(Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)²

Here, Hypotenuse = OP, Base = Tangent length, Perpendicular = Radius

**Calculation:**

Using Pythagoras theorem:

OP² = Tangent² + Radius²

⇒ 25² = Tangent² + 7²

⇒ 625 = Tangent² + 49

⇒ Tangent² = 625 - 49

⇒ Tangent² = 576

⇒ Tangent = √576

⇒ Tangent = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: AB is parallel to CD. A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively, and ∠PEB = 42°. G is a point between AB and CD such that ∠BEG = 21° and ∠GFE = 34°. What is the measure of ∠EGF?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB is parallel to CD.

A transversal PQ intersects AB and CD at E and F, respectively.

∠PEB = 42º

G is a point between AB and CD such that:

∠BEG = 21º

∠GFE = 34º

Concept used:

Sum of angles on a straight line is 180o.

Sum of all angles of a triangle is 180o.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96a986d27c9fc484cd9d5724d031efea62c00ee5992b45c0a5c2b57f3a7a35e9.png]

Now , In triangle EGF,

⇒ 34o + ∠EGF + 117o = 180o 

⇒ ∠EGF = 180o - 117o - 34o 

⇒ ∠EGF = 29o 

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: POR is the diameter of a circle. PQ and RQ are its two chords. The length of arc PQ is half of the length of arc RQ. Find the measure of ∠POQ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

POR is the diameter of a circle.

PQ and RQ are two chords.

Length of arc PQ = (1/2) × Length of arc RQ

**Formula used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is directly proportional to the length of the arc.

Angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba8c93fbc25bf6a04a55fbe51fcb17e561d16493633de7f192186194f7594688.png] 

Let the angle subtended by arc PQ at the center O be ∠POQ = x degrees.

Let the angle subtended by arc RQ at the center O be ∠ROQ = y degrees.

Given that the length of arc PQ is half of the length of arc RQ.

Since the angle at the center is proportional to the arc length, we have:

∠POQ = (1/2) × ∠ROQ

⇒ x = (1/2)y

⇒ y = 2x

Since POR is the diameter, it is a straight line passing through the center O.

Therefore, the angles on the straight line POR add up to 180 degrees.

∠POQ + ∠ROQ = 180 degrees

⇒ x + y = 180

Substitute the value of y = 2x into the equation:

⇒ x + 2x = 180

⇒ 3x = 180

⇒ x = 180 / 3

⇒ x = 60 degrees

So, ∠POQ = 60 degrees.

**∴ The measure of ∠POQ is 60 degrees.**

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, ∠P, ∠Q, ∠R, and ∠S taken in order are in the ratio 2 : 8 : 3 : 7. Which type of quadrilateral is PQRS?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The angles in quadrilateral PQRS, ∠P, ∠Q, ∠R, and ∠S are in the ratio 2 : 8 : 3 : 7.

**Formula used:**

Sum of angles of any quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculations:**

Let the angles be 2x, 8x, 3x, and 7x.

⇒ 2x + 8x + 3x + 7x = 360°

⇒ 20x = 360°

⇒ x = 18°

Now, the angles are:

∠P = 2x = 36°, ∠Q = 8x = 144°, ∠R = 3x = 54°, ∠S = 7x = 126°.

Since the sum of opposite angles is not equal, the quadrilateral is a trapezium.

**∴ The correct answer is option (2) Trapezium.**

questions.question: Find the co-ordinates of the centroid of a triangle whose vertices are A(1, 4), B(7, 8) and C(10, 12).

B = (7, 8)

**Formula used:**

The co-ordinates of the centroid (G) of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), and (x₃, y₃) are given by:

G = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) / 3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) / 3)

x₂ = 7, y₂ = 8

x₃ = 10, y₃ = 12

x-coordinate of the centroid:

⇒ x = (1 + 7 + 10) / 3

⇒ x = 18 / 3

⇒ x = 6

y-coordinate of the centroid:

⇒ y = (4 + 8 + 12) / 3

⇒ y = 24 / 3

⇒ y = 8

**∴ The co-ordinates of the centroid of the triangle are (6, 8).**

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 53° and ∠B = 46°. The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O. What is the measure of ∠DOC?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In quadrilateral ABCD:

∠A = 53°

∠B = 46°

The bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at O.

**Formula used:**

Sum of interior angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f723285f96a4f562aa9fd1ca803d54d99d892dd93bb01032bc93e34013341f0.png] 

In quadrilateral ABCD, the sum of all interior angles is 360°.

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 53° + 46° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 99° + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 360° - 99°

⇒ ∠C + ∠D = 261° ......(1)

Consider the triangle DOC.

Since CO bisects ∠C, then ∠OCD = ∠C / 2

Since DO bisects ∠D, then ∠ODC = ∠D / 2

In ∆DOC, the sum of angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠DOC + ∠OCD + ∠ODC = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + (∠C / 2) + (∠D / 2) = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + (∠C + ∠D) / 2 = 180°

Substitute the value from equation (1):

⇒ ∠DOC + 261° / 2 = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC + 130.5° = 180°

⇒ ∠DOC = 180° - 130.5°

⇒ ∠DOC = 49.5°

**∴ The measure of ∠DOC is 49.5°.**

questions.question: If (3, 2) are coordinates of the centroid of a triangle, whose vertices are (0, 4), (-2, 0) and (p, 2), then find the value of p.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Centroid coordinates = (3, 2)

Vertices of triangle = (0, 4), (-2, 0), (p, 2)

**Formula used:**

Centroid formula: ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/(3), (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/(3))

**Calculation:**

Given centroid = (3, 2)

Using formula:

⇒ (0 + (-2) + p)/(3) = 3 and (4 + 0 + 2)/(3) = 2

For x-coordinate:

⇒ (-2 + p)/(3) = 3

⇒ -2 + p = 3 × 3

⇒ -2 + p = 9

⇒ p = 9 + 2 = 11

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 32.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 4 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
questions.solution:
**Given**

∠STR = 32.5°.

The bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at the point T

The ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 4 ∶ 9

**Calculation**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd361e24cb54aa2c7406ab284d943597339ee12e81993afbb92bb2b02f51e1a2.png] 

∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360° 

∠P + ∠Q = 360 - (∠R + ∠S) ..(1)

∠STR + ∠R/2 + ∠S/2 = 180

2∠STR = 360 - (∠R + ∠S) ..(2)

Compare Equation (1) and (2):

∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q)/2

∠P + ∠Q = 32.5 × 2 = 65°

Let the ∠P and ∠Q = 4x and 9x

(4x + 9x) = 65°

13x = 65° 

x = 5° 

The difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P = 9x - 4x = 5x = 5 × 5° = 25°.

**The correct answer is Option (4).**
